added.title: Senior Product Manager, AI-Native Legal Platform
added.description:
About Laurel Employment Law

We are not your traditional law firm. Laurel Employment Law is a fully remote, tech-driven, AI-native law firm that's redefining how employment law is practiced. We're a team of smart, ambitious people who collaborate to deliver outstanding results for our clients - and we have fun doing it!

We use cutting-edge legal tech to eliminate inefficiencies, empower autonomy, and give our team the freedom to focus on what matters: winning for our clients and building meaningful careers. If you thrive in a high-performance, growth-oriented culture and want to do your best work without commuting, micromanagement, or outdated systems, this is the place for you.

The Role

We're hiring a Senior Product Manager to lead the next phase of our custom legal platform - taking it from active build into full-scale rollout across the firm. You'll own the roadmap, prioritization, and execution as we expand its capabilities, working closely with engineering and firm leadership to turn a strong foundation into the operating backbone of how we work.

Alongside the core platform, you'll spin up no-code AI pilots that automate and improve day-to-day operations - testing what works, then folding proven wins back into the main build.
We're looking for a hands-on business builder and systems thinker who sees internal operations software not as a super function, but as a competitive engine. If you want to shape a platform already in motion, not just start from zero, this is that seat.

The Culture

Laurel is built different. We started the Firm asking an important question: "what if it didn't have to suck to work at a law firm? In fact, what if it could be kind of awesome?" The result is an award-winning culture where we take the work seriously without ever taking ourselves too seriously. We've built a team of winners who work together to get more done, more efficiently, while leaving competitors asking themselves, "how the heck did they do that?" We win and we have fun doing it. It's a better way to build.

What You'll Do

Own the strategy, development, and scaling of our custom operational platform from concept to launch.
Partner closely with engineering and firm leadership to define and execute the product roadmap.
Design, build, and ship functional AI agents into production that automate core legal workflows.
Spin up no-code AI pilots using workflow automation tools to test and improve how the firm runs.
Use SQL and data analysis to inform product decisions and measure impact.
Navigate the practical realities of building product within a heavily regulated industry.
Operate as a hands-on business builder - comfortable moving from strategy to execution and back.
Own additional initiatives to extend and support the broader Laurel Platform beyond custom builds.

Your Skills & Mindset

Proven track record launching 0-to-1 products; prior early-stage startup experience strongly preferred.
Practical experience navigating and delivering value within heavily regulated sectors such as legal, finance, or healthcare.
Strong analytical background with hands-on proficiency in SQL and data analysis.
Direct experience building, testing, and shipping functional AI agents into production.
General familiarity with no-code and workflow automation platforms like Make or similar tools.
You get things done - fast, without hand holding, and without losing sight of quality.
Creative, strategic thinker who thrives in a remote-first, tech-savvy team.
Motivated, ambitious, radically optimistic, and driven to grow your impact and your career.

Why Laurel

Fully Remote
— work from anywhere in the US with world-class collaboration tools.
Tech-Enabled Efficiency
— we use automation, dashboards, and smart systems so you can focus on building, not admin.
Culture That Wins Together
— no egos, no bureaucracy- just sharp, driven people who push and support each other.
Competitive Compensation
— base salary of $140,000–$185,000.
Paid time off, holidays, health insurance, referral bonuses, and real opportunities for advancement.

Come Shape the Future of Legal Technology

If you want to build product at the highest level — remotely, intelligently, and collaboratively — come build with us. Laurel Employment Law is where talented product builders thrive, grow, and win.

Amazon Demand Tech Products helps marketers, sellers, and app developers promote their products across mobile, CTV, and the open internet at scale. You will drive our product strategy of our Display, Video, and Audio ad buying system end to end leading product and business strategy across a team of product managers, engineers, and applied scientists to deliver industry leading customer results for marketers and app developers of all shapes and sizes.

The Demand Tech Products team sits at the intersection of ad tech, large-scale data infrastructure, and applied ML. Our systems process billions of bid requests daily, fusing multiple shopping and app signal sources to determine where an impression opportunity is coming from and whether we should show an advertiser's ad to that consumer at that time to maximize the probability that they will be interested in buying a product, subscribing to a service, completing a lead, or installing an app or purchasing within that app. The challenge is that the ad industry is changing rapidly with AI and chat agent usage, understanding how shoppers and consumers use apps, websites, and watch CTV for daily utility, shopping, news, or entertainment is noisy and evolving quickly. Your job is to build products to help marketers and app developers run successful campaigns across this rapidly evolving space.

Key job responsibilities

Continue to build and improve our performance campaign products and services
Strike or improve partnerships with advertisers, agencies, publishers, measurement providers, and data providers that will improve our performance products.
Lead product ideation, building, and launches across a team of product managers, engineers, and applied scientists to function as a single threaded team focused on a single customer obsessed objective.

Experience leading engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product

added.title: Head of Fraud Product
added.description:
Who We Are

Sardine is the leading agentic risk platform for fighting financial crime. Our integrated solution unifies data across risk teams to help organizations stop fraud in real time, prevent AI-driven attacks, and automate fraud and AML operations. Sardine’s platform is strengthened by one of the fastest-growing fraud consortiums in the market, spanning more than 6 billion profiled devices, 800 million consumers, and 3 million businesses worldwide. Leading companies including FIS, GoDaddy, Intuit, Edward Jones, ZoomInfo, and Checkout.com rely on Sardine to secure and grow trust in their products.

Our Culture

We have hubs in the Bay Area, NYC, Austin, Toronto, and São Paulo. However, we maintain a remote-first work culture. #WorkFromAnywhere
We hire talented, self-motivated individuals with extreme ownership and high growth orientation.
We value performance and not hours worked. We believe you shouldn't have to miss your family dinner, your kid's school play, friends get-together, or doctor's appointments for the sake of adhering to an arbitrary work schedule.

Location:

Remote - United States
From Home / Beach / Mountain / Cafe / Anywhere!
We are a remote-first company with a globally distributed team. You can find your productive zone and work from there.

About The Role

We are seeking a deeply experienced and visionary Head of Fraud Product to lead the strategy, development, and execution of Sardine’s core fraud prevention suite. In this role, you will own the end-to-end product lifecycle for our fraud solutions, ensuring we stay multiple steps ahead of bad actors.

You will lead a talented team of product managers and collaborate tightly with engineering, data science, risk operations, and go-to-market teams. The ideal candidate is a seasoned product leader with a relentless passion for risk management, a deep understanding of the payments ecosystem, and a proven track record of building scalable, data-driven enterprise products.

What You'll Be Doing

Set the Vision & Strategy: Define and execute the roadmap for Sardine’s fraud product portfolio, balancing immediate customer needs with long-term strategic innovation in device intelligence, behavioral biometrics, and machine learning.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner directly with Engineering and Data Science leaders to translate complex fraud typologies into highly accurate, low-latency models and product features.
Optimize Core Metrics: Drive product improvements that maximize fraud catch rates while minimizing false positives and user friction for our merchants.
Market & Threat Intelligence: Stay relentlessly up-to-date on emerging fraud trends, account takeover (ATO) tactics, synthetic identity creation, and competitor capabilities to ensure Sardine maintains its market-leading edge.
Go-to-Market Enablement: Work closely with Marketing and Sales to define product positioning, value propositions, and sales enablement materials.

What You'll Need

Experience: 10+ years of product management experience, with at least 5+ years in a leadership role managing other PMs.
Domain Expertise: Deep, hands-on experience in payment fraud at a high-growth payment processor, fraud-vendor company or merchant.
Industry Background: Prior experience working at a specialized fraud vendor or B2B SaaS startup.
Analytical Rigor: Exceptional ability to work with large datasets. You are comfortable defining, tracking, and optimizing complex risk metrics (e.g., recall, precision, approval rates).
Execution Focus: A bias for action and a proven track record of taking zero-to-one products to market and scaling them to enterprise readiness.
Communication Skills: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex technical and risk concepts to both highly technical and non-technical stakeholders (including C-suite clients).

Benefits We Offer

Generous compensation in cash and equity
Early exercise for all options, including pre-vested
Work from anywhere: Remote-first Culture
Flexible paid time off and Year-end break
Health insurance, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents - US and Canada specific

MacBook Pro delivered to your door
One-time stipend to set up a home office — desk, chair, screen, etc.
Monthly meal stipend
Monthly social meet-up stipend
Annual health and wellness stipend
Annual Learning stipend

added.title: Principal Product Operations Manager
added.description:
Why Socure?

Socure is building the identity trust infrastructure for the digital economy — verifying 100% of good identities in real time and stopping fraud before it starts. The mission is big, the problems are complex, and the impact is felt by businesses, governments, and millions of people every day.

We hire people who want that level of responsibility. People who move fast, think critically, act like owners, and care deeply about solving customer problems with precision. If you want predictability or narrow scope, this won’t be your place. If you want to help build the future of identity with a team that holds a high bar for itself — keep reading.

Principal Product Operations Manager

About The Role

Product Operations exists to give product teams the systems, data, and processes they need to plan, prioritize, and deliver well — the same way Sales Ops supports Sales or DevOps supports Engineering. This role sits at the center of that discipline, owning four things: the tools and systems
product teams plan and work in, the reporting and analytics
that give everyone visibility into what's happening, the process
that makes planning and delivery repeatable instead of reinvented pod by pod, and the ongoing work of keeping strategy and execution connected
as priorities shift.

We run Product Operations as a hybrid centralized/embedded model
: some Product Ops work sits centrally and serves every product team consistently, while other Product Ops work sits embedded inside individual product lines, close to their day-to-day priorities. This role sits in the centralized hub — you're the shared systems, process, and reporting engine that every embedded product manager and product ops partner relies on, rather than being dedicated to any single product line.

We're a small team, so this role is intentionally broad. At larger companies, "owns the tools," "owns the reporting," and "owns the process" are sometimes split into two or three separate roles. Here, one person does all of it, with the flexibility to shift emphasis as priorities and team size change over time.

What You'll Do

Own the product systems & tools stack

Administer and configure the core product management / roadmapping platform (e.g., Aha!, Productboard, or equivalent) — workspaces, fields, workflows, scorecards, and permissions.
Own the connection between the product management platform and the engineering work-tracking system (e.g., Jira) — field mapping, status sync, and keeping data consistent between the two.
Manage the broader product tech stack: evaluate new tools, prevent tool sprawl, and maintain integrations across roadmap, delivery, feedback, and CRM systems.
Build and maintain the intake and prioritization workflows product teams use to submit, score, and rank requests.
Document system configuration and standard operating procedures so system knowledge isn't concentrated in one person (including yourself).

Support reporting & analytics for the Product Org

Build and maintain the dashboards and reports that give leadership and embedded product teams a reliable view of roadmap status, delivery progress, and portfolio health.
Define and track core product operations metrics (e.g., cycle time, roadmap adherence, planning hygiene, tool adoption).
Centralize and facilitate Product Performance metrics definition, telemetry builds, and availability to central data and BI teams, and coordinate dashboard and reporting builds with the central Business Intelligence team to enable deeper insights and faster decision making for the Product Team.
Partner with Finance, Sales/RevOps, and Engineering to bring commercial and delivery data (e.g., CRM/ARR data) into product prioritization and reporting.
Support recurring reporting cadences — business reviews, quarterly/annual planning, board updates — with clean, trusted data.
Monitor data quality and drive hygiene standards across the systems that feed reporting.

Drive process, efficiency & team enablement

Design and document repeatable processes for planning, prioritization, intake, and roadmap reviews — so teams have a consistent way of working instead of reinventing it pod by pod.
Identify friction points and manual, duplicative work in the product development lifecycle, and fix them — through better process, automation, or tooling.
Build templates, playbooks, and checklists (e.g., for feature intake, roadmap reviews, launch readiness) that save product managers time and reduce administrative burden.
Act as the go-to resource for product managers and embedded product ops partners on how to use shared tools and processes effectively — training, office hours, documentation.
Facilitate cross-functional handoffs between Product, Engineering, Design, and GTM so work moves smoothly instead of stalling on a handoff.
Continuously look for opportunities to standardize process across pods while leaving room for the flexibility each team actually needs.

Keep strategy and execution aligned

Partner with product leadership to translate high-level strategy and company priorities into a concrete, trackable roadmap and planning cadence.
Run the rhythm of planning — quarterly/annual planning cycles, roadmap reviews, and business reviews — that keeps execution connected to strategy as priorities shift.
Monitor progress against strategic priorities and flag early when day-to-day execution is drifting from what leadership actually intended.
Support trade-off and prioritization conversations when competing asks conflict with stated strategic priorities, so decisions get made deliberately rather than by default.
Make sure work happening inside individual pods visibly ladders up to company-level strategic themes, not just local priorities.
Close the loop after major planning moments — make sure decisions made in a review actually get reflected in the systems everyone works from day to day.

What You Bring

10+ years in Product Operations, Business/Sales Operations, or a Product Analyst/Management role, ideally supporting or working inside of a product or engineering organization.
Hands-on experience working in or familiarity with a product roadmapping/PPM tool (e.g., Aha!, Productboard, Jira Product Discovery) and a work-tracking tool (e.g., Jira, Linear, Azure DevOps).
Comfort building dashboards and reports (in the PPM tool itself, Tableau, Looker, or Google Sheets/Excel); SQL is a plus.
Use of LLM-based tools (e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, Perplexity, etc.) to augment and optimize job and role-related workflows, dashboards, research, etc.
Experience designing and documenting repeatable processes — intake, prioritization, planning cadences — rather than just running an existing one.
Working knowledge of PDLC and SDLC processes — roadmaps, backlogs, sprints, and prioritization frameworks (e.g., RICE, WSJF), different types of launch and product profiles (0-1 products, mature products, etc) and the PDLC process to support them.
Comfort facilitating conversations where strategic priorities and day-to-day execution are in tension, and helping stakeholders land on a decision.
Strong analytical skills — able to turn messy or scattered data into something people can act on.
A generalist mindset and genuine comfort moving between technical configuration, process design, and data/reporting work in the same week.
A bias toward noticing inefficiency and fixing it, even when it falls outside the "official" scope of the role.
Excellent documentation and communication skills — you're the connective tissue between central leadership and embedded product teams.
Ability to work autonomously on a small, fast-moving team where priorities shift.

Why This Role Matters

Product teams move faster and make better decisions when the systems, process, and data behind their work are trustworthy. Without a dedicated owner, strategy and execution tend to drift apart — teams stay busy, but on priorities that no longer reflect what leadership actually needs. In a centralized/embedded Product Ops model, this role is the connective tissue: it's why a PM on any pod can trust the roadmap data, why a planning decision made in a leadership review actually shows up in what gets built next sprint, and why leadership can get a straight answer about where things stand. As the team grows, this role can naturally split into two or three — Systems & Tools, Process, and Data & Analytics — but today it's one person who can support all of it.

added.title: Director, Product Operations
added.description:
About the Role

The hiring organization is seeking a Director, Product Operations to lead operational infrastructure, cross-functional alignment, and release execution across key product initiatives. Sitting at the intersection of product, engineering, and go-to-market teams, this role is responsible for driving program coordination, establishing disciplined release management processes, and supporting executive-level customer engagement to ensure the timely delivery of high-quality product releases.

This is a full-time, 100% remote role based in the United States.

Key Responsibilities

Own the end-to-end program plan for new product launches across product, engineering, sales, marketing, implementation, and support.
Keep cross-functional teams aligned and accountable for delivering workstreams and milestones on schedule.
Identify dependencies and blockers early, driving resolution across teams without direct reporting authority.
Assist the organization in distinguishing critical requirements from secondary features under time constraints, ensuring commitments are met.
Establish and maintain standard operating procedures, communication rhythms, and documentation practices that scale across products and release cycles.
Introduce structure and guardrails to release processes to minimize customer-impacting issues while maintaining release velocity.
Administer product operations tooling and analytics platforms to support team workflows.
Own the product metrics framework across adoption, engagement, retention, and business impact to guide prioritization and resource allocation.
Design and launch an executive-level customer council.
Establish a structured, recurring schedule for the customer council that optimizes executive participants' time and generates actionable input for product direction.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in business, computer science, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
7+ years of experience in product operations, technical program management, or related roles within B2B or enterprise software companies.

added.title: Principal Product Operations Manager
added.description:
Why Socure?

Socure is building the identity trust infrastructure for the digital economy — verifying 100% of good identities in real time and stopping fraud before it starts. The mission is big, the problems are complex, and the impact is felt by businesses, governments, and millions of people every day.

We hire people who want that level of responsibility. People who move fast, think critically, act like owners, and care deeply about solving customer problems with precision. If you want predictability or narrow scope, this won’t be your place. If you want to help build the future of identity with a team that holds a high bar for itself — keep reading.

Principal Product Operations Manager

About The Role

Product Operations exists to give product teams the systems, data, and processes they need to plan, prioritize, and deliver well — the same way Sales Ops supports Sales or DevOps supports Engineering. This role sits at the center of that discipline, owning four things: the tools and systems
product teams plan and work in, the reporting and analytics
that give everyone visibility into what's happening, the process
that makes planning and delivery repeatable instead of reinvented pod by pod, and the ongoing work of keeping strategy and execution connected
as priorities shift.

We run Product Operations as a hybrid centralized/embedded model
: some Product Ops work sits centrally and serves every product team consistently, while other Product Ops work sits embedded inside individual product lines, close to their day-to-day priorities. This role sits in the centralized hub — you're the shared systems, process, and reporting engine that every embedded product manager and product ops partner relies on, rather than being dedicated to any single product line.

We're a small team, so this role is intentionally broad. At larger companies, "owns the tools," "owns the reporting," and "owns the process" are sometimes split into two or three separate roles. Here, one person does all of it, with the flexibility to shift emphasis as priorities and team size change over time.

What You'll Do

Own the product systems & tools stack

Administer and configure the core product management / roadmapping platform (e.g., Aha!, Productboard, or equivalent) — workspaces, fields, workflows, scorecards, and permissions.
Own the connection between the product management platform and the engineering work-tracking system (e.g., Jira) — field mapping, status sync, and keeping data consistent between the two.
Manage the broader product tech stack: evaluate new tools, prevent tool sprawl, and maintain integrations across roadmap, delivery, feedback, and CRM systems.
Build and maintain the intake and prioritization workflows product teams use to submit, score, and rank requests.
Document system configuration and standard operating procedures so system knowledge isn't concentrated in one person (including yourself).

Support reporting & analytics for the Product Org

Build and maintain the dashboards and reports that give leadership and embedded product teams a reliable view of roadmap status, delivery progress, and portfolio health.
Define and track core product operations metrics (e.g., cycle time, roadmap adherence, planning hygiene, tool adoption).
Centralize and facilitate Product Performance metrics definition, telemetry builds, and availability to central data and BI teams, and coordinate dashboard and reporting builds with the central Business Intelligence team to enable deeper insights and faster decision making for the Product Team.
Partner with Finance, Sales/RevOps, and Engineering to bring commercial and delivery data (e.g., CRM/ARR data) into product prioritization and reporting.
Support recurring reporting cadences — business reviews, quarterly/annual planning, board updates — with clean, trusted data.
Monitor data quality and drive hygiene standards across the systems that feed reporting.

Drive process, efficiency & team enablement

Design and document repeatable processes for planning, prioritization, intake, and roadmap reviews — so teams have a consistent way of working instead of reinventing it pod by pod.
Identify friction points and manual, duplicative work in the product development lifecycle, and fix them — through better process, automation, or tooling.
Build templates, playbooks, and checklists (e.g., for feature intake, roadmap reviews, launch readiness) that save product managers time and reduce administrative burden.
Act as the go-to resource for product managers and embedded product ops partners on how to use shared tools and processes effectively — training, office hours, documentation.
Facilitate cross-functional handoffs between Product, Engineering, Design, and GTM so work moves smoothly instead of stalling on a handoff.
Continuously look for opportunities to standardize process across pods while leaving room for the flexibility each team actually needs.

Keep strategy and execution aligned

Partner with product leadership to translate high-level strategy and company priorities into a concrete, trackable roadmap and planning cadence.
Run the rhythm of planning — quarterly/annual planning cycles, roadmap reviews, and business reviews — that keeps execution connected to strategy as priorities shift.
Monitor progress against strategic priorities and flag early when day-to-day execution is drifting from what leadership actually intended.
Support trade-off and prioritization conversations when competing asks conflict with stated strategic priorities, so decisions get made deliberately rather than by default.
Make sure work happening inside individual pods visibly ladders up to company-level strategic themes, not just local priorities.
Close the loop after major planning moments — make sure decisions made in a review actually get reflected in the systems everyone works from day to day.

What You Bring

10+ years in Product Operations, Business/Sales Operations, or a Product Analyst/Management role, ideally supporting or working inside of a product or engineering organization.
Hands-on experience working in or familiarity with a product roadmapping/PPM tool (e.g., Aha!, Productboard, Jira Product Discovery) and a work-tracking tool (e.g., Jira, Linear, Azure DevOps).
Comfort building dashboards and reports (in the PPM tool itself, Tableau, Looker, or Google Sheets/Excel); SQL is a plus.
Use of LLM-based tools (e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, Perplexity, etc.) to augment and optimize job and role-related workflows, dashboards, research, etc.
Experience designing and documenting repeatable processes — intake, prioritization, planning cadences — rather than just running an existing one.
Working knowledge of PDLC and SDLC processes — roadmaps, backlogs, sprints, and prioritization frameworks (e.g., RICE, WSJF), different types of launch and product profiles (0-1 products, mature products, etc) and the PDLC process to support them.
Comfort facilitating conversations where strategic priorities and day-to-day execution are in tension, and helping stakeholders land on a decision.
Strong analytical skills — able to turn messy or scattered data into something people can act on.
A generalist mindset and genuine comfort moving between technical configuration, process design, and data/reporting work in the same week.
A bias toward noticing inefficiency and fixing it, even when it falls outside the "official" scope of the role.
Excellent documentation and communication skills — you're the connective tissue between central leadership and embedded product teams.
Ability to work autonomously on a small, fast-moving team where priorities shift.

Why This Role Matters

Product teams move faster and make better decisions when the systems, process, and data behind their work are trustworthy. Without a dedicated owner, strategy and execution tend to drift apart — teams stay busy, but on priorities that no longer reflect what leadership actually needs. In a centralized/embedded Product Ops model, this role is the connective tissue: it's why a PM on any pod can trust the roadmap data, why a planning decision made in a leadership review actually shows up in what gets built next sprint, and why leadership can get a straight answer about where things stand. As the team grows, this role can naturally split into two or three — Systems & Tools, Process, and Data & Analytics — but today it's one person who can support all of it.

About The Role

This role defines how Posh Live shows up to buyers and sellers - shaping positioning, messaging, and go-to-market strategies that drive adoption, engagement, and growth for Poshmark's live shopping product.

Through deep customer engagement with multifamily operators, you'll uncover needs, validate ideas, and ensure we're building products that solve real problems.

We're looking for someone who can think broadly about where our product portfolio should go, then roll up their sleeves to make it happen.

The strongest product managers at ApartmentIQ share a few consistent behaviors:
Deep customer empathy:
You stay close to customers and build real relationships, not just collect feedback. You invest the time in conversations, follow-ups, and context to understand what’s actually driving their decisions and pain.

Bias for speed and action:
Velocity is your north star. You make fast, sound calls, ship the smallest thing that proves value, then iterate based on what users actually do.
Obsession with quality and details:
You have strong product taste and a high bar. You sweat the small stuff because that is what makes the product feel reliable, premium, and easy to use.
Decisive judgment:
You can operate in ambiguity and make hard tradeoffs without dragging the team through endless debate. Once the decision is made, you communicate it clearly and align everyone behind it.
Relentless drive:
You push through blockers and find paths forward. You do not accept “can’t” as an endpoint, and you keep delivering meaningful customer value even when constraints show up.

About the role

You own the subscription funnel from the moment a user encounters Centr through their first 30 days of paid usage. Web pages between ad click and trial start, in-app onboarding through first workout, offer architecture at trial end, cancellation, and the in-app surfaces that drive equipment upsell once they're a subscriber. You'll work next to the Sr. Ecom Manager (storefront, CRM, bundle), our growth agency (paid acquisition), and the Core UX product team (long-term in-app experience).

A dedicated full-stack web engineer is paired to you, and the two of you ship the web funnel autonomously. Paywalls and pricing iterate via RevenueCat config without dev tickets. Native mobile work routes through Core UX engineering, so part of your job is making the case for prioritization rather than assuming the capacity.

We move these numbers by building experiences worth converting on. Our read is that the funnel underperforms because the experience does, not because we haven't pushed hard enough. We'd rather earn a subscription than trap someone into one. Get the experience right and the numbers follow.

What you'll own

Web subscription onboarding. Signup, assessment, paywall, offer, trial activation. Closing the conversion gap between web and mobile is a first-90-days priority.
QR-to-app landing. The post-scan experience for retail equipment buyers (Costco, Academy) and bundle buyers.
In-app activation. Install through day 7. Onboarding flow, day-0/1/3 nudges, push, in-app engagement during trial.
Trial-to-paid conversion. Offer architecture at trial end, in-app re-engagement, cancellation on web and in-app, win-back surfaces inside the product.
Pricing and packaging. Plan architecture across iOS, Android, and web. Differentiated offers for new vs. returning vs. lapsed users.
In-app equipment upsell. The shopping feature, placement, and surfacing logic that turns subscribers into bundle and equipment buyers.

What success looks like

Web trial conversion closes a meaningful share of the gap to mobile
iOS install → paid conversion improves materially against today's baseline
A QR-to-app flow we're excited to point Costco and Academy traffic at
An in-app equipment upsell surface producing measurable attach from existing subscribers
A cancellation flow that recovers a respectable share of would-be churners
CAC payback shortened enough that paid spend can scale with confidence

You should apply if

You've owned a subscription funnel end-to-end and moved trial-to-paid at consumer scale
You've shipped against both mobile (iOS/Android) and web subscription flows and understand why they behave differently
You know where the landmines are in RevenueCat, App Store / Play Store, Stripe, and Recharge
You believe the best growth work is indistinguishable from the best product work. You move trial-to-paid by making the trial deliver value, not by hiding the cancel button
You're effective at influencing roadmaps you don't own (a meaningful chunk of your highest-leverage work lives inside the Core UX roadmap)
You spend more time in Claude Code than anyone you know

This might not be the right fit if

Your experience is all with mature, well-instrumented funnels. Building one from zero is a different muscle, and this role is mostly the zero-to-one kind
You love CRO and landing-page work but don't want to own pricing, paywalls, and trial design alongside it
You'd rather hit targets with pressure tactics than earn them through the experience
You want to own strategy and hand off execution. Here you'd do both
You want a proven playbook to run. We're still writing ours, and that's the fun of it

Why this role

Centr's subscription business has the brand, the content, the equipment, and the HYROX tailwind. What it's missing is someone to own the funnel that ties them together. If building that sounds like the best problem you could be working on, we'd like to meet you.

Centr, LLC is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values inclusion. Centr, LLC welcomes individuals of all backgrounds and experiences to apply.

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

We are hiring Staff & Principal Product Data Scientists to help build a world-class data ecosystem that supports and scales data-driven product decision-making at Slack.

As Staff & Principal Product Data Scientists, you will work closely with cross-functional partners to define the product landscape, derive actionable insights, and directly shape product strategy. You’ll partner with Product, Design, and Engineering (PDE), as well as Go-To-Market (GTM) teams, to contribute directly to product development—shaping what we build, how we measure success, and how we iterate.

You will also play a pivotal role in designing and developing Slack’s agentic data delivery platform. By connecting the dots across our data backend, metrics foundations, and insights analyses, you will help us achieve true data self-serve capabilities within an AI and agentic context.

At Slack, we foster a positive, diverse, and supportive culture. We look for people who are curious, bold, and eager to improve every day. Our team values being smart, humble, hardworking, and above all, collaborative.

What you will be doing:

Establish strong partnerships with product stakeholders to identify opportunities, prioritize roadmaps, and implement execution excellence.
Evangelize evidence-based decision-making by partnering with key leaders and driving the general accessibility of data and insights.
Perform evidence-based evaluations of the most important drivers for increased adoption of Slack product capabilities.
Build key success metric frameworks and self-serve reporting to monitor Slack product health.
Prototype foundational data models and partner with Data Engineering functions to elevate these into canonical sources of truth.
Contribute to the design and implementation of Slack's agentic data delivery platform.
Quantitatively identify potential product opportunities to improve user experiences and unlock business value.
Partner closely with Product Researchers to align roadmaps and collaborate on projects to answer complex questions.

What you should have:

5+ years of experience in product data science in related tech industries.
A consistent record of using data to drive product teams to achieve ambitious goals and influence company-level outcomes.
Advanced proficiency in SQL and at least one programming language for data science, such as Python, R, or Scala. Knowledge of workflow orchestration tools like Apache Airflow is highly desirable.
Strong foundation in statistics, experimentation, causal inference, ML, and analytical problem-solving.
Experience working with large-scale data technologies such as Spark, Presto, Hive, Hadoop, or similar distributed data platforms.
Proven ability to communicate complex analytical findings clearly to executive and cross-functional audiences.
A related degree required. A BS degree in a quantitative field (e.g., Computer Science, Economics, Physics); an advanced degree (MS, PhD) is a strong plus.

Unleash Your Potential

When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best , and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best . Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.
